head: abfc477c1cad64c4885125e7cf10830fdc94e540
label: task153-outbox-batch-end-mark-sent-semantics
purpose: Adjudicate ONLY whether 'mark SENT once at batch end' (batching the per-row conditional markSent of the F03 outbox relay) can enter a performance experiment under the EXISTING spec semantics. Not an optimization: no production relay/Mapper change, no switch, no c100x2000 load, no default change, no throughput/P99 claim. Counterexample-first: per-row baseline vs a test-only simulated batch-end update on an isolated scratch MySQL with the real DDL and the real Mapper SQL, with programmably simulated sends (never Mockito-faked DB results).

reasons: Unauthorized duplicate-delivery window widening: crash after all 3 rows were broker-accepted shows baseline next-round re-send scope = 1 row (the in-flight one) vs candidate = 3 rows (= whole batch, upper bound = batch-size 100); a second instance's real selectPendingBatch also selects the already-delivered-but-unmarked rows.

SENT visibility delayed: baseline independent-connection snapshots between sends are [SENT,PENDING,PENDING] then [SENT,SENT,PENDING]; candidate keeps the whole batch [PENDING,PENDING,PENDING] until batch end.

sent_at time semantics drift: baseline drift from that row's send-completion moment = 0s,0s with a 4s gap between rows; candidate drift = 3s,3s with a 0s gap (whole batch flattened), contradicting the DDL comment 'sent_at = 投递成功时间'.

Aggregate-only attribution: per-row markSent returns 0/1 per row; the batch conditional UPDATE returns only an aggregate count (2 ids, 1 hit -> 1, cannot tell which row missed), and on a real SQL failure the whole batch of already-delivered rows stays PENDING (re-send scope = whole batch) with a different exception type than the per-row path.

Consumer-side SETNX / business anchors do NOT constitute authorization: the spec authorizes only 'same eventId re-delivered -> business executes once'; it does not authorize the delivery side to enlarge the duplicate window, and dedup removes side-effect duplication, not the extra network re-delivery, the extra next-round load, or the in-DB indistinguishability of delivered vs not-delivered rows.
verdict.note: Consumer-side idempotency was explicitly NOT treated as authorization; the four difference classes above each hit the task's stop conditions.

baselineFacts.selectSql: SELECT * FROM verify_event_outbox WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND retry_count < #{maxRetry} ORDER BY id LIMIT #{limit}
baselineFacts.markSentSql: UPDATE verify_event_outbox SET status = 'SENT', sent_at = NOW() WHERE id = #{id} AND status = 'PENDING'
baselineFacts.incrRetrySql: UPDATE verify_event_outbox SET retry_count = retry_count + 1 WHERE id = #{id} AND status = 'PENDING'
baselineFacts.relayLoop: per-row ascending by id; syncSend success -> immediate conditional markSent; send failure -> incrRetry + continue; mark failure -> incrRetry + counted failed; exhausted guard keeps row untouched
baselineFacts.relayTransaction: VerifyOutboxRelay.relay() has NO @Transactional; each markSent/incrRetry is an independent auto-commit call
baselineFacts.crashModel: relay catches only Exception, so an Error escapes; at most the single in-flight row can be 'sent but unmarked' in the baseline
baselineFacts.eventId: generated and stored at outbox insert time; relay re-sends reuse the row's eventId byte-for-byte
baselineFacts.consumerIdempotency: eventId SETNX (24h TTL) plus business anchors (verification_result PK, leaderboard_contribution.record_id PK state machine)

specHardConstraints: 判定事件经待发行表投递: PENDING row first, then relay delivers and marks SENT; consumer's eventId equals the row's eventId byte-for-byte
投递失败保留行: failure -> retry_count+1 and stays PENDING for next round; above threshold keep the row for manual handling, never silently drop
事件幂等消费: same eventId re-delivered -> SETNX dedup, business executes once
判定/终判事件 SHALL NOT be sent synchronously on the decide thread; relay is the sole exit
existingObservationsNoSpecText: SENT becomes visible on a separate connection immediately after that row's send returns (per-row auto-commit)
sent_at is approximately that row's send-completion moment
at most 1 row is 'sent but unmarked' at a crash (the in-flight one)
markSent returning 0 rows is discarded by relay and still counted as success
stillNeedsProductDecision: widening the duplicate-delivery window from <=1 row to <=batch-size
changing sent_at from per-row delivery-completion time to a batch-end timestamp (affects docs/perf/归因-*.md lag analysis)
delaying SENT visibility to batch end and losing per-row attribution of the batch mark (ops/manual-handling view)

candidate.protocol: sendPhaseBatchEnd: same select SQL/order/exhausted-guard/failure incrRetry as the production relay, but successful rows are NOT marked during the send phase; after the phase a test-only batch conditional UPDATE (UPDATE ... SET status='SENT', sent_at=NOW() WHERE status='PENDING' AND id IN (...), via PreparedStatement; deliberately NOT added to the production mapper) marks the set of successfully sent ids

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: crash after the k-th send and before the batch-end mark widens the next-round re-scan scope
designedCounterexamples.evidence: baseline nextRound=[crash-e3]; candidate nextRound=[crash-e1, crash-e2, crash-e3]; extraReSendRows=2; row's eventId unchanged; no new rows inserted

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: already-delivered-but-unmarked rows are indistinguishable to a second instance -> duplicate delivery plus aggregate mark loses attribution
designedCounterexamples.evidence: secondInstanceSelection=[multi-e1, multi-e2]; second instance marks row 1 on a separate connection; batch aggregate affected=1, cannot identify which row was already marked

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: mixed batch: a failed send is marked SENT or interrupts later rows
designedCounterexamples.evidence: both paths: failed row stays PENDING, retry_count 0->1, sent_at NULL; exhausted row untouched; candidateSent=2 (excludes failed and exhausted); nextRound=[mix-e2] both paths

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: one real batch UPDATE SQL failure leaves all delivered rows PENDING
designedCounterexamples.evidence: real failure via temporary table rename; batchFailureType=java.sql.SQLSyntaxErrorException vs singleFailureType=org.apache.ibatis.exceptions.PersistenceException; rows f1/f2 stay PENDING and nextRound=[cond-e3, cond-e4] (= whole batch); single path re-sends only the same one row on next round in its equivalent case

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: conditional UPDATE '0 rows / partial hit' cannot be attributed per row at batch granularity
designedCounterexamples.evidence: aggregateAffected=1 for [1 PENDING + 1 already-SENT id]; all-SENT batch 0; nonexistent id 0; existing relay behavior kept: markSent 0-row return discarded, summary 'success=1, failed=0'

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: sent_at drifts from the row's own send-completion moment and the batch is flattened
designedCounterexamples.evidence: baseline drift=0s,0s, baseline gap=4s; candidate drift=3s,3s, candidate gap=0s (each simulated send holds 3000ms)

designedCounterexamples.counterexample: exhausted rows are selected or marked by the candidate
designedCounterexamples.evidence: exhaustedRow test: next-round real select SQL returns empty; candidate send phase returns 0 ids; empty batch UPDATE affects 0 rows; row untouched by both paths
